question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed immutable, persisted `sessions_spawn.tools` contract—including `"none"`, deny-wins rules, and CLI rejection of deny-based policies—as the supported per-spawn isolation API?
rationale: This establishes a new security-sensitive user-facing tool-policy surface and durable child-session behavior; source review can evaluate mechanics but cannot choose the permanent product and compatibility contract.

options.title: Sponsor the persisted policy contract
options.body: Confirm `tools` as the supported API, then require current-head behavior proof and removal of the release-owned changelog edit before merge.

options.title: Narrow the feature first
options.body: Keep only a smaller allow-only or embedded-runtime-only contract if the broader deny and CLI semantics are not intended to become public API.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open for security and product design until the desired isolation model is explicitly settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the persisted policy contract
recommendation.body: Confirm `tools` as the supported API, then require current-head behavior proof and removal of the release-owned changelog edit before merge.
